newsitem.title: UK: Deadlocked N.Irish talks adjourn for election.
newsitem.headline: Deadlocked N.Irish talks adjourn for election.

text.p: Northern Ireland's multi-party peace talks were adjourned on Wednesday after nine months of deadlock, their chairman, former U.S. senator George Mitchell, announced.

They were suspended to allow the province's Protestant and Catholic parties to prepare for a general election which Prime Minister John Major must call for the British mainland and Northern Ireland by May 22, Mitchell said.

Mitchell said "the Easter holiday period will be followed in. quick succession by a general election in the United Kingdom and district council elections in Northern Ireland. The independent chairmen propose that the next plenary session be held on Tuesday, June 3."

Britain and Ireland launched the talks last June in a bid to defuse conflict about British rule. But they have been plagued by acrimony between the parties and overshadowed by growing IRA guerrilla violence.
Sinn Fein, the Irish Republican Army's political wing, is barred because the guerrillas are waging an escalating campaign to unite the largely Protestant province with Catholic Ireland.
